name: Question 6
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007650/assets/c6496d117c1b769474c353b0bfeef6836d21f080fb108752d55b8bb090dc0243.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(-5,-3),$ and passes through the point $(7,9).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-5,-3),$ and so we have

$$
x+5=p{t}^{2},\,y+3=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(7,9),$ we can substitute $x=7$ and $y=9$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}12=p{t}^{2} \\ 12=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =2pt \\ 6 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{6}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =p{(\frac{6}{p})}^{2} \\ 12 & =p\cdot \frac{36}{{p}^{2}} \\ 12 & =\frac{36}{p} \\ p & =\frac{36}{12} \\ p & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+5=(3){t}^{2},\,y+3=2(3)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+5=3{t}^{2},\,y+3=6t.
$$

Question 6
?

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the parabola shown above?

a
x+3=3t2,y+5=6t
b
x+5=6t2,y+3=3t
c
x+5=3t2,y+3=6t
d
x+3=6t,y+5=3t2
e
x+5=−3t2,y+3=−6t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at (−5,−3), and passes through the point (7,9).

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

In our case, (h,k)=(−5,−3), and so we have

x+5=pt2,y+3=2pt.

Since the parabola passes through (7,9), we can substitute x=7 and y=9 into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

{12=pt212=2pt.

Solving the second equation for t, we have

12=2pt6=ptt=6p.

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for p, we get

12=p(6p)212=p⋅36p212=36pp=3612p=3.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x+5=(3)t2,y+3=2(3)t,

which simplify to

x+5=3t2,y+3=6t.
